title: A PORTION FOR THOSE WHO SERVE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From the Israelites' half, select one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys, sheep or other animals. Give them to the Levites, who are responsible for the care of the Lord's tabernacle. So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord commanded Moses. - Num 31:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The community's half also had a portion set apart — this time for the Levites, who cared for the tabernacle. The Levites owned no land and depended on the offerings of the people for their support. God made sure that those who devoted themselves to His service were provided for through the generosity of everyone else.

This is a principle that runs right through Scripture. Those who give themselves to serving God's people should be supported by God's people. Paul applies exactly this idea in the New Testament, teaching that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from it (1 Cor 9:13-14). It is not about making ministers wealthy; it is about the whole family of God sharing the load so that the work can continue.

Notice too the simple obedience: "Moses and Eleazar did as the Lord commanded." No arguing, no adjusting the instructions to suit themselves — just faithful obedience. That is a quiet example for all of us. When God has made His will clear, our part is to obey, trusting that His instructions are wise and good.

Behind all of this is a God who provides. He cared for the Levites through His people, and He cares for us through His Son, who gives us everything we need for life and godliness (2 Pet 1:3). We serve and give within a family held together by the provision of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How can you support those who serve God's people around you?
2. Is there an area where God has spoken clearly and simply needs your obedience?
3. Where have you seen God provide for you through others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful Provider, thank You for caring for Your servants and for me. Make me generous toward those who serve, and quick to obey what You have made clear. Amen.
